isolation: hello-api exposes a single stateless GET /greeting endpoint with no per-caller data, so isolation is by identity: each scenario acquires its own fresh OAuth2 authorization-code+PKCE token via Thunder SSO (the test-caller account) and asserts only on the response to its own request. Only one test account (test-caller) was provisioned on the roles gate ticket, so the 'Jordan' caller in the fixed-message rule is represented by a second, independently-acquired token for the same account rather than a distinct identity — noted as a limitation, not a defect.

scenarios.rule: Only a signed-in caller may request the greeting
scenarios.scenario: A signed-in caller receives the greeting

steps.text: Sam has signed in via Thunder SSO
steps.command: browser: authorization_code+PKCE flow at http://development-idp.openchoreo.localhost:8080/oauth2/authorize (client_id from the roles-gate ticket, scope=greeting:read) signed in as test-caller/**** via the IdP sign-in form, then POST /oauth2/token exchanged the code for an access token
steps.observed: token endpoint returned 200 with an access_token scoped 'greeting:read'

scenarios.rule: Only a signed-in caller may request the greeting

steps.command: no token was acquired or attached to the request

scenarios.scenario: The greeting does not vary between callers

steps.text: Sam and Jordan have both signed in via Thunder SSO
steps.command: two independent authorization_code+PKCE flows against http://development-idp.openchoreo.localhost:8080/oauth2/authorize, each signed in via the IdP form (test-caller/****) with its own PKCE verifier/challenge and state, each exchanged at POST /oauth2/token
steps.observed: two distinct access tokens issued (distinct jti claims)

steps.text: Sam requests the hello-world greeting and Jordan requests the hello-world greeting
they receive the same greeting message
steps.observed: both responses were exactly {"message":"Hello, world!"} — no diff
